blocks.content: Two patterns cover what is required and what is not. **なければなりません** states that something must be done. **なくてもいいです** is its inverse : the action is not required.

left.label: なければなりません
left.description: Must do : the action is an obligation. Formal, used in writing and polite speech.
left.example_jp: 薬を毎日飲まなければなりません。
left.example_en: I have to take medicine every day.

right.label: なくてもいいです
right.description: Don't have to : the action is optional. Giving permission not to do something.
right.example_jp: 今日は来なくてもいいです。
right.example_en: You don't have to come today.

lines: [Neg. stem] + **なければなりません**   ← must (formal / polite)
[Neg. stem] + **ないといけません**     ← must (casual spoken)
[Neg. te-form] + **もいいです**        ← don't have to

rows.japanese: 明日までにレポートを出さなければなりません。
rows.romaji: Ashita made ni repōto wo dasanakereba narimasen.
rows.english: I must submit the report by tomorrow.

rows.japanese: もっと練習しないといけません。
全部食べなくてもいいですよ。
rows.romaji: Zenbu tabenakute mo ii desu yo.
rows.english: You don't have to eat everything.

rows.japanese: ネクタイをしなくてもいいです。
rows.romaji: Nekutai wo shinakute mo ii desu.
rows.english: You don't need to wear a tie.

blocks.content: なきゃ and なくちゃ are heavily contracted casual forms of なければならない : you will hear them constantly in everyday speech and anime. They are not appropriate in formal writing.
